text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem Brotherhood calls for constitutional reforms and lifting curbs on public freedoms; Jordan's Islamist party studying boycott of parliamentary elections due later in the year in coordination with the other secular opposition parties.
- Defence urges military court to acquit Jordanian soldier charged with premeditated murder of seven Israeli schoolgirls, pleading his mental state.
- Crown Prince says at start of Medpartenariat fair held in Amman that economic cooperation should not take the place of political breakthroughs.
- Blue-chip Arab Bank stock leads trading in the Amman stock exchange and dealers expect its price to breach the 300 dinar ($423) level pushing the official index higher.
- Moslem Brotherhood says its boycott call of the coming parliamentary elections is the first step towards a national programme to be agreed with other opposition parties.
- Islamic Action Front (IAF) deliberations fail to unify positions on elections.
